question: What Settings localization contract should OpenClaw support for schema/uiHint-derived config labels, and how should the two open partial Settings localization PRs be sequenced?
rationale: UI chrome can follow the existing t() and generated-locale pipeline, but schema-derived labels require a maintainer-owned key shape and fallback behavior across config schema metadata and Control UI rendering.

options.title: Define one Settings i18n contract
options.body: Choose a single key/fallback design for Settings chrome, section metadata, Quick Settings, and schema labels, then ask the open PRs to rebase or be replaced against it.

options.title: Land low-risk chrome slices first
options.body: Accept narrow toolbar or Quick Settings localization PRs after proof, while keeping schema-derived labels explicitly open on this issue.

options.title: Defer schema-label localization
options.body: Limit current work to non-schema UI chrome and document that schema/uiHint labels remain English until a later config metadata design.

recommendation.title: Define one Settings i18n contract
recommendation.body: Choose a single key/fallback design for Settings chrome, section metadata, Quick Settings, and schema labels, then ask the open PRs to rebase or be replaced against it.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has adjacent Settings/config history and is the best available owner for the UX/API tradeoff between config schema metadata and Control UI localization.
